page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highcpu-60 is a compute-optimized server instance powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9B14 processor. It features 60 dedicated vCPUs derived from 30 physical cores with multithreading enabled at 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 118 GB of RAM, providing approximately 1.97 GB of memory per core. Cache specifications include 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPUs, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and specialized compute performance. The instance achieves top 25% results in stress-ng multi-core CPU tests and PassMark CPU scores. Extended instruction sets such as AVX-512, including AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, along with cryptography flags like AES, VAES, and SHA_NI, contribute to strong performance in PassMark extended instructions and encryption tests. Memory bandwidth for small cached blocks is highly efficient at 4252.27 GB/sec, though uncached large-block read and write speeds fall into the average range at 146.01 GB/sec and 53.0 GB/sec respectively.

This hardware configuration is designed for compute-heavy workloads such as software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing, where it registers strong benchmark scores. It also demonstrates high throughput for Redis SET operations and database operations. However, the lower memory-to-vCPU ratio and the lack of local storage represent clear tradeoffs for memory-intensive databases or large-scale storage-bound applications. For machine learning, it handles prompt processing and text generation efficiently for smaller models, but performance drops to average tiers when running larger 70B parameter models.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highcpu-60 is an x86_64 compute-optimized server instance configured with 60 dedicated vCPUs and 118 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor. Lacking bundled local storage and GPU accelerators, this instance is designed for high-compute density. It delivers strong multi-core performance, as shown by its stress-ng multi-core score of 86108.26 and PassMark CPU score of 68289.24. Hardware support for AVX-512 and advanced cryptography instructions drives strong results in encryption and extended instruction benchmarks. While cached memory bandwidth is highly efficient, uncached large-block memory operations and large-model LLM inference perform in the average tier. This resource profile is highly suited for compute-bound workloads like software compilation, ray tracing, and high-throughput Redis operations, though the low memory-to-core ratio of 1.97 GB represents a clear tradeoff for memory-intensive applications.
